description: Building complete Java applications with desktop and web front ends: object-oriented design, abstract classes and interfaces, JavaFX and event handling, servlets and JavaServer Pages, JDBC with MVC, and JavaBeans, ending with a deployed web application on a database. Taught to the depth of a leading enterprise Java development course.
modelledOn: Horstmann, Core Java (Volumes I and II)
Murach, Murach's Java Servlets and JSP
Jakarta EE Servlet, JSP and JDBC specifications
outcomes: Apply object-oriented principles, abstract classes, interfaces and design patterns to structure a large program.
Build desktop interfaces with JavaFX, scene graphs, layouts, properties and event handling.
Write servlets that handle HTTP requests, sessions, cookies and filters.
Connect to a relational database with JDBC and structure the application as model, view and controller.
Use JavaBeans, scopes and attributes to share state across a web application.
Generate dynamic pages with JavaServer Pages, JSTL and expression language, and deploy to a servlet container.

units.title: Classes, objects and OO principles
topics: Review: classes, constructors, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, static and instance members
SOLID principles; cohesion and coupling; composition over inheritance
Generics, collections and streams in application code; Optional and immutability
Unit testing with JUnit and mocking; Maven project structure and dependencies
Packaging, modules and documentation

units.title: Abstract classes and interfaces
topics: Abstract classes versus interfaces; default and static methods; functional interfaces and lambdas
Programming to an interface; dependency injection by hand
Design patterns: Strategy, Observer, Factory, Builder, Template Method, Singleton, DAO
Refactoring a monolithic program into layered components

units.title: JavaFX basics
topics: JavaFX architecture: Application, Stage, Scene, the scene graph; running with the JavaFX SDK
Controls: labels, buttons, text fields, lists, tables, dialogs; layouts: HBox, VBox, GridPane, BorderPane
FXML and Scene Builder; CSS styling of JavaFX; images, charts and media
Properties and bindings; observable collections
Building a desktop client for a student records or inventory system

units.title: Event-driven programming
topics: Event sources, handlers, event types; lambdas as handlers; the event dispatch chain
Mouse, keyboard, action and change events; drag and drop
Threading in GUIs: the JavaFX application thread, Task and Service for background work
Animation and timelines; responsiveness

units.title: Java servlets
topics: The servlet container (Tomcat or Jetty); the servlet life cycle; HttpServlet and the request/response objects
Handling GET and POST, parameters, headers, redirects, forwarding; the deployment descriptor and annotations
Sessions, cookies, URL rewriting; filters and listeners
Error handling, logging and security basics (input validation, output escaping, HTTPS)
File uploads and asynchronous servlets in brief

units.title: SQL, JDBC and MVC
topics: JDBC drivers, connections, statements, prepared statements, result sets, transactions; connection pooling
The DAO pattern and a data access layer; mapping rows to objects
MVC for web applications: controller servlets, model classes, JSP views
SQL injection and prepared statements; handling concurrency and errors
Introduction to JPA/Hibernate as the next step

units.title: JavaBeans, scopes and attributes
topics: JavaBean conventions: properties, getters and setters, serialisation
Request, session, application and page scopes; storing and retrieving attributes
Passing data between servlets and JSPs; form beans and validation
Thread safety of shared attributes

units.title: JavaServer Pages
topics: JSP life cycle and translation to servlets; directives, scriptlets (and why to avoid them), declarations
Expression language and the JSTL core, formatting and SQL tags
Custom tags and tag files; templating and includes; internationalisation
Comparison with modern alternatives: Thymeleaf, REST APIs with JSON and a JavaScript front end

units.title: Project and deployment
topics: Assembling a complete web application: authentication, CRUD, reports, MVC, database
Building a WAR, configuring Tomcat, deploying to a cloud VM; environment configuration
Testing the web layer; performance and security review
Project presentation and code review

schedule.title: Object-oriented foundations and SOLID design
schedule.exercise: Review a short class hierarchy for a student fees system and write one paragraph naming which SOLID principle each class violates and how you would repair it.

tasks.title: Write a Java Account class with encapsulated balance, a constructor and two subclasses, then print polymorphic results for five sample accounts
Rewrite a loop-based report of 20 student marks using streams, Optional and an immutable record, and check that the output matches the original
Refactor a given fee calculator that breaks open-closed and single responsibility into composed classes, then add a new fee type without editing existing code

schedule.title: Testing, Maven and packaging
schedule.exercise: Write a short README for a small Java library explaining its Maven layout, how to run the tests and how to generate its documentation.

tasks.title: Write five JUnit-style tests for a Grade calculator class, run them and fix the one failing boundary case
Use a hand-written mock of a payment gateway interface to unit test a Checkout class for success, decline and timeout paths
Draw a package and module dependency diagram for a three-layer student records project and justify which packages should be exported or hidden

schedule.title: Interfaces, patterns and layered refactoring
schedule.exercise: Choose two design patterns from this week and write a half-page comparison of when each is the right tool, using a school or market example.

tasks.title: Define a Discount functional interface and apply three lambdas to a list of 10 prices, comparing the printed totals with hand calculations
Implement Strategy and Factory so a fare calculator for tro-tro routes selects peak, off-peak or student pricing by name, and test all three
Split a 150-line monolithic inventory program into UI, service and DAO layers using hand injection, keeping every original output identical

schedule.title: JavaFX controls, layouts and FXML
schedule.exercise: Sketch on paper three screen layouts for a student records app and name the JavaFX layout pane you would choose for each region.

tasks.title: Model a JavaFX Stage, Scene and scene graph as Java classes and print the tree for a window with a root, one label and one button
Design a login and registration form using GridPane inside BorderPane, labelling every control and drawing the nesting hierarchy as a diagram
Write an FXML-style layout description and a CSS-like style table for a dashboard, then parse both to print a styled component tree

schedule.title: Properties, bindings and a desktop client
schedule.exercise: Write a short design note listing the properties and observable collections a student records client needs and which views bind to each.

tasks.title: Create a simple observable property class, bind two instances so one mirrors the other, and print the values after five changes
Implement an observable list with change listeners and use it to keep a total-marks label updated as 10 records are added and removed
Design the SQL schema for an inventory system, load 20 sample items, and write the queries the desktop client's table view would use for search and low-stock alerts

schedule.title: Events, threading and animation
schedule.exercise: Explain in a paragraph why long database calls on the UI thread freeze an application and sketch the Task and Service fix.

tasks.title: Implement an event source, handler interface and lambda handlers for a Button class, and print the dispatch order for three registered handlers
Simulate a GUI thread with a background Task that processes 100 records in batches and posts progress updates without blocking the event loop
Build a timeline of keyframes that animates a progress value from 0 to 100, then tune frame timing so the update count stays under a given budget

schedule.title: Servlet container, requests and sessions
schedule.exercise: Trace by hand the life of one GET request through a servlet container, listing which life-cycle methods run and in what order.

tasks.title: Write a minimal servlet class with init, service and destroy methods in a mock container and log the life-cycle calls for three requests
Implement doGet and doPost handlers for a registration form in the mock container, covering parameters, a redirect and a forward
Add a session-tracking filter that counts visits per cookie, expires idle sessions after a limit, and prove it with a scripted sequence of 12 requests

schedule.title: Servlet errors, logging and security
schedule.exercise: Review a given servlet for input validation and output escaping flaws and list five fixes in order of risk.

tasks.title: Add input validation and HTML escaping to a comment servlet and show that a script tag submitted as input is rendered harmless
Implement an error-handling filter that maps exceptions to error pages and writes structured log lines, then verify the log for four failing requests
Simulate a file upload handler that enforces size and type limits and stores files under generated names, and test it with six crafted uploads

schedule.title: JDBC, DAO and MVC
schedule.exercise: Draw the sequence of calls from a controller servlet through the model and DAO to the view for a product listing page.

tasks.title: Write the SQL for a students table, insert 10 rows and run parameterised queries mirroring a JDBC PreparedStatement, checking the row counts
Implement a StudentDAO with find, save and delete over an in-memory store and a row-to-object mapper, and test it with 15 records
Design the MVC structure for a library web app, assigning each controller, model class and view to a diagram and tracing a borrow request

schedule.title: SQL injection, concurrency and JPA
schedule.exercise: Write a short explanation, for a junior developer, of why prepared statements stop SQL injection while string escaping often does not.

tasks.title: Exploit a deliberately vulnerable login query with a crafted string, then rewrite it with bound parameters and confirm the same input now fails
Run two interleaved transactions that withdraw from one mobile money wallet, show a lost update, then fix it with a locking or isolation choice
Map a Student and Course pair of tables to annotated entity classes in a mock ORM and compare the generated queries with hand-written JDBC

schedule.title: JavaBeans, scopes and shared state
schedule.exercise: List which data in a shopping cart application belongs to request, session and application scope and justify each choice.

tasks.title: Write a StudentBean following JavaBean conventions with getters, setters and serialisation, then round-trip it to a string and back
Create a form bean with validation that maps request parameters to fields and returns error messages for six deliberately bad submissions
Expose a race on a shared application-scope visit counter using multiple threads, then fix it with synchronisation and compare final counts over 1000 hits

schedule.title: JSP, EL, JSTL and modern alternatives
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page comparison of server-rendered JSP pages and a REST API with a JavaScript front end for a clinic booking system.

tasks.title: Translate a small JSP page by hand into the servlet code it becomes, marking directives, scriptlets and expressions in the result
Replace scriptlets in a product list view with EL and JSTL-style loops and conditionals, and verify identical output for 8 products
Build a custom tag that renders a formatted price in cedis and use it in a templated page with a shared header include in two languages

schedule.title: Capstone web application and deployment
schedule.exercise: Prepare a ten-minute project demo script and a review checklist that a classmate can use to code review your application.

tasks.title: Create the database schema and seed data for a student portal with users and roles, and write the CRUD and report queries the app needs
Write tests for the controller and DAO layers of the capstone app and report coverage, fixing any untested error path found
Deploy a packaged web application to a cloud VM with environment variables for the database URL, then recover from a deliberately bad configuration
